**Reasoning**: The current score plateau comes from all candidates being greedy-Steiner variants with similar structure. Adding the shortest-path-tree candidate diversifies the starting set, and running local search on the top 3 candidates (rather than 1) lets the re-grafting neighborhood explore different basins — often one of the runner-up trees improves below the former best. Runtime stays well within limits since improve() is bounded at 6 rounds of Dijkstra re-runs.
